# Automatic transmission fluid change

> **Some safety-critical values on this page are not confirmed** (marked [Unverified] or [Partial]): they come from one source or are only partly supported. Verify against the factory service manual before use; later runs re-check them against new sources.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Drain transmission fluid and fill with new Nissan Matic S ATF while an assistant shifts through each gear. [t34]

Drain the automatic transmission pan, refill with fresh fluid, and consider a poor man's flush. [t92]

Locate the green knob dipstick, undo its securing bolt, pull it up, then rotate it to read the fluid level. [t488]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Optionally do the bypass first by swapping the two hoses shown, one of them at the bottom of the radiator on the passenger side.
2. Loosen the bolt located on the bottom of the transmission pan.
3. Allow the old fluid to drain out completely from the pan.
4. [Unverified value] Reinstall and torque the pan bolt down to 25 ft-lbs.
5. [Unverified value] Add 4 or 5 quarts of Matic-S through the dipstick fill tube in the engine bay; its cap comes off with a 10mm socket.
6. Remove the hose from the supply transmission line and attach a longer extension hose to it.
7. Submerge the end of that extended hose into a bucket to catch the fluid.
8. Have a helper run the truck until the fluid coming out of the hose turns red.
9. [Unverified value] Pour the remaining 6 or 7 quarts of Matic-S back into the transmission through the dipstick tube using a funnel.
10. Check the fluid level.
11. Run the shifter through all the gears with the truck off.

_Procedure reported by [t34]; 5 steps reworded by a reviewer. Photos of this job are in the source: <https://www.thenewx.org/threads/how-to-transmission-pmf-poor-mans-flush-pbr.30213/>_

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t34] [Partial]</summary>

1. Drain the old transmission fluid from the pan into a container.
2. [Partial] Attach clear hose to the supply line at the exit of the OEM radiator cooler (or dipstick tube).
3. [Partial] Fill the reservoir with new fluid through the dipstick tube until it reaches full capacity.
4. [Partial] Have an assistant shift through each gear while you monitor the output for color change.
5. Repeat filling and shifting cycles until the draining fluid turns a bright red.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t92] [Partial]</summary>

1. Drain the automatic transmission pan to remove old fluid.
2. Refill the transmission with fresh fluid.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t488] [Partial]</summary>

1. Locate the green knob dipstick on the left side of the engine.
2. Undo the 10mm bolt securing the dipstick tube.

</details>

## Tools

- Clear hose [t34]
- Hose clamps (spring or screw type) [t34]
- 5-gallon plastic jugs [t34]
- [Partial] Bright light [t34]
- [Partial] 10mm socket or wrench [t488]

## Parts

- [Partial] Crush washer: Same type as oil pan plug [t92]
- [Partial] [Unverified value] Nissan Matic S ATF: 12 quarts recommended [t34]
- Veggie oil jug, optional [t34]

## Specifications

- **Dipstick tube bolt size**: 10mm [t488] ([Unverified] single report)
- **Initial fill amount via dipstick tube**: 4 to 5 quarts [t34] ([Unverified] single report)
- **Transmission pan bolt torque**: 25 ft-lbs [t34] ([Unverified] single report)

## Tips & gotchas

- Use a 5-gallon fast-food veggie oil container to catch fluid and keep the garage clean. [t34]
- Monitor color change by looking through clear hose or using a bright light. [t34]
- [Partial] [Unverified value] Ensure you fill exactly half of a standard 5-gallon jug (approx. 12 quarts) for proper measurement. [t34]
- Consider a 'poor man's flush' to extract fluid from the torque converter and valved-off portions of the body for better results than a simple drain. [t92]
- Pull up the dipstick and rotate it 90 degrees to read the fluid level. [t488]

## Common mistakes

- Draining too quickly without shifting gears, leaving old fluid trapped in specific paths. [t34]
- [Partial] Running the pump dry by not filling enough before starting the engine cycle. [t34]
